questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place where they speak English in order to make the study easier for myself. I also chose the destination because I thought that the courses in the university sounded really interesting and relevant for my education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was fairly easy. The host university was good at sending out information on what to do next. And the website for the host university also had a lot of information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the beginning of my stay I was invited to several orientation meetings where they told us about the social life at the university and the academics and life as an exchange student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think that the process of finding housing was pretty stressful especially because of the covid19 situation. I did not want to pay a lot of money in advance in case I would not be able to go, but at the same time, the different places for housing were booked pretty quickly which limited my opportunities. I feel like there were quite a lot of opportunities for housing, but I would have liked to have been guided a bit more in my search for accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I ended up living at a brand new student accomodation about 3,5 km away from campus. It was a bit far away but I got used to it and ended up liking to take the walk to and from campus. There were also several buses going directly to campus, and it was also possible to rent bikes. For me living off campus worked totally fine and it also became a place outside of campus to meet people. However, I think that many of the student accommodations that were available when I booked were quite expensive, and I also ended up paying around 900 euro a month. I would therefore recommend looking into the different possibilities not too late in the planning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For my destination I think there was generally a lack of affordable student accommodation and that the places were filled very quickly, and I would have liked more help in this process.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think that the registration process was pretty easy to complete. However, I felt like the deadline for choosing courses was close to when classes actually started, and therefore I think the process can be kind of confusing and a bit stressful if you do not get approved to take the courses. Luckily this did not happen in my case

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The host university sent out quite detailed descriptions on how to register. You would register for the courses you wanted. Later you would have to check that the timetable for the various courses matched up and you would maybe have to change some of your courses to make it work. You would also be given some time to try out your chosen courses and then have the opportunity to change them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were people at the host university that you could ask for help if you had questions about the registration. For example I was a bbit confused about the timetables, and they helped me with that.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up only being able to take one of the courses that I was originally planning on taking, since the courses change and some get canceled, and some of them did not match up with their different timetables. However, I ended up really liking all of my courses!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I would just say to check your mails regularly for updates and guides to register and to ask for help if you are unsure of something or try to find the answers at the host university's website.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think that there were quite many interesting courses and that the lecturers were good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think that because it was in English for me it automatically made it a bit more difficult to understand certain things in the courses. However, I  do not think that it was so difficult that I could not follow, and generally, I feel like the level was about the same as at the University of Copenhagen. I feel like there was perhaps a bit less reading per week compared to what I am used to, but at the same time there were also more assignments (I had two courses that were worth 10 ECTS which each contained two assignments or an assignment and a presentation, and then two courses that were 5 ECTS points and each consisted of one assignment). The assignments were generally between 2500-3000 words. I feel like I had a lot of free time in the beginning of the semester, and then later on I ended up being a bit stressed about studying for and doing all of the assignments. Therefore I would say that it is a good idea to make sure to read up on some of the texts in each subject as you go along and think of what you might want to do in your assigments, so that you do not get too stressed in the end.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the style of teaching was somewhat similar to that of UCPH. However, my courses were lecturers in which it was possible to ask questions but other than that it was mostly the lecturer talking. I did not have any group work or something like that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Aspects of Irish Folklore (5 ECTS) which is about beliefs and customs in Ireland which I really liked!
I also took the courses Sociology of Memory, Trauma & Collective Denial (10 ECTS) which was also quite interesting. I also took the course Race, Ethnicity, Migration and Nationalism (10 ECTS) which I also liked. And then I had a course called Sexuality and Society (5 ECTS), and I enjoyed this course as well.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of my courses and would recommend them to others. I feel some of the courses were somehow connected to each other and also that they each provided me with new insights that I feel I could use in my own studies.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I think that living in my destination was generally quite expensive. I definitely ended up spending more money on beer than I had expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think that everything was maybe a bit more expensive than what I had imagined

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs and societies that you could join which I think was pretty great. However, some of the clubs for example had a lot of members and therefore you would have to book sessions sometimes weeks in advance.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were clubs which consisted of different sports. There were also societies which consisted of many different kinds of interests that people could join. And there were various happenings at campus for students to get engaged in

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I ended up not making so much use of the opportunities of clubs and societies, but I think that they are probably a good way to meet people. I was also told that it is a good way to meet more of the Irish students instead of mainly other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend looking into opportunities of going on different day trips and also setting aside maybe some weekends to explore other parts of the country. I did this several times and these experiences were some of the highlights of my exchange

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I don't think it was too hard, but of course, some things were different from what I am used to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend joining some clubs and societies and generally just going around the city and checking out what it has to offer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was really anything that was very challenging in terms of the cultural differences. But of course it could sometimes be a bit challenging having to speak English all of the time. I was also sometimes a bit confused by the Irish accent

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think that people were generally friendly and I really enjoyed meeting up at some of the local pubs with the people I met

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to meeting people:) You could for example try to join some clubs and societies and different kinds of groups for exchange students.
Make use of the opportunities that the university and the city offers and explore it.
Just see it as an opportunity to meet many different people from other cultures, to improve your English and in general learn more, both academically but also about yourself!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check your emails daily and to make use of the facilities offered at the university.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I thought it was pretty scary in the beginning because I was going to travel alone and live in a country where I don't know anyone, but it feels great that I have done it and know that it is something that I can do. 
I am also really happy that I got to see more of the country and experience the culture more and get to share it with other people.
And I also feel like it has made speaking English feel a bit more natural to me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was especially challenging in the beginning when I had to meet a lot of people, and it was even more challenging to do in English. But I also feel like it has been good for me to experience. And people were very nice and just as nervous and eager to meet other people!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
